lesson: At the restaurant: ordering food (A0 · Lesson 4)

cards.definition: The thing you sit at to eat in a restaurant.
cards.example:
- A table for two, please.
Uma mesa para dois, por favor.
cards.note: Ao chegar: a table for two. O garçom responde this way — “por aqui”.

cards.definition: The paper or card with all the food and the prices.
cards.example:
- Can I have the menu, please?
Pode me trazer o cardápio, por favor?
cards.note: Fala-se “MÉ-niu”, não “menú”. O cardápio de bebidas é o drinks menu.

cards.definition: To tell the waiter what food you want.
cards.example:
- I want to order now, please.
Eu quero pedir agora, por favor.
cards.note: Verbo e substantivo: I order e my order. O garçom pergunta are you ready to order?

cards.definition: Food that comes from the sea or a river.
cards.example:
- The fish is very good here.
O peixe é muito bom aqui.
cards.note: Plural igual ao singular: one fish, two fish. Nunca “fishes” no prato.

cards.definition: The most common meat on a menu.
cards.example:
- I eat chicken every day.
Eu como frango todo dia.
cards.note: Incontável quando é a comida: I eat chicken, sem artigo. Com artigo vira o animal vivo.

cards.definition: The paper that says how much you have to pay.
cards.example:
- The bill, please. We are ready.
A conta, por favor. Estamos prontos.
cards.note: Na Inglaterra bill, nos Estados Unidos check. Os dois funcionam nos dois lugares.

cards.definition: The polite way to ask for anything in a restaurant or a shop.
cards.example:
- Can I have the menu, please?
Pode me trazer o cardápio, por favor?
cards.note: A fórmula mais útil da viagem inteira. Serve para tudo: Can I have water? Can I have the bill?

cards.definition: What you say when you finish and want to pay.
cards.example:
- The bill, please. Card, thank you.
A conta, por favor. Cartão, obrigado.
cards.note: Não precisa de frase longa. Duas palavras e o please resolvem, e é o que o nativo diz.

cards.definition: The meal you eat in the middle of the day. It is NOT a small snack.
cards.example:
- We have lunch at one o'clock.
Nós almoçamos à uma hora.
cards.note: “Lanche” é snack! Lunch é a refeição do meio-dia, com prato e tudo.

cards.definition: Italian food made of flour: spaghetti, penne. It is NOT a folder for papers.
cards.example:
- I want pasta with the fish.
Eu quero macarrão com o peixe.
cards.note: “Pasta” de guardar papel é folder! No cardápio, pasta é sempre macarrão.

exercise.title: At the restaurant: ordering food (A0 · Lesson 4)

questions.explanation: Fixed phrase: a table FOR two.
“Ready TO” + verb. Portuguese pulls a “for” that is wrong here.
One fish, two fish — the plural does not change.
Food in general takes no article: “I eat chicken”.
“Account” is a bank account. In a restaurant it is the bill.
The most useful phrase of the whole trip.
“Lanche” is a snack. Lunch is the midday meal.
On a menu, pasta is always food — never a folder.
